title: What Is Lettermail? Canada Post's Letter Service
description: Lettermail is Canada Post's service for ordinary letters and cards: what it covers, size and weight limits, prices, delivery standards and what it lacks.
answer: Lettermail is Canada Post's service for ordinary letters and cards: anything you post with stamps in an envelope, up to 500 grams. A standard letter up to 30 grams costs $1.24 with a booklet stamp or $1.44 with a single stamp, and is delivered in two to four business days. It has no tracking and no signature.

blocks.p: Lettermail covers letters, cards and flat items that are posted with stamps or metered postage and fit within Canada Post's size and weight limits: up to 245 x 156 x 5 mm and 50 g for a standard letter, and up to 380 x 270 x 20 mm and 500 g for non-standard and oversize items. Anything larger or heavier moves to parcel services. The exact limits and how to measure an envelope are in [Lettermail size and weight limits](/blog/lettermail-size-and-weight-limits).

rows: Standard letter, over 30 g up to 50 g
Non-standard or oversize, up to 100 g

blocks.p: These are Canada Post's prices without tax. A Permanent stamp is always accepted at the current domestic rate. See [letter rates by weight](/blog/canada-post-letter-rates-by-weight), and [what is known about a 2027 increase](/blog/stamp-price-2027-what-we-know).

Canada Post's delivery standards for letters are two business days locally, three within a province and four across Canada. They are not guaranteed and can be affected by holidays and seasonal volume. See [how long a letter takes](/blog/how-long-does-a-letter-take-in-canada).

An ordinary letter has no tracking number, no signature on delivery and no proof of mailing, and Canada Post says individual letters without tracking numbers cannot be investigated. For those, Registered Mail adds $13.15 to the postage. See [can you track a letter in Canada](/blog/can-you-track-a-letter-canada) and [Registered versus regular mail](/blog/registered-vs-regular-mail-canada).

Businesses that send more than 1,000 items can qualify for Incentive Lettermail, which saves about a cent on a standard letter. Most small senders pay the ordinary price. See [Canada Post letter discounts](/blog/canada-post-bulk-letter-discount).
A letter ordered online is printed, stamped and posted as ordinary Lettermail. See [how online letter mailing works](/blog/how-online-letter-mailing-works).
